headline: Keep your Mac session awake.
summary: A discreet menu bar utility that simulates tiny mouse micro-movements when you are idle — so a screen share, a long meeting, or a waiting job does not lose the login session to sleep or lock.
differentiator: Guard starts Inactive at every launch. You turn it on for this session — until you stop it, or until a timed session ends.
featuresSubtitle: Everything you need to keep a login session alive — without becoming a bulky stay-awake suite.

features.title: Menu bar status
features.text: Outline shield when Inactive, filled when Active, remaining time during a Timed Session, slashed shield if Accessibility is missing.

features.title: True user activity
features.text: Mouse movement and keyboard key-down reset idle. Micro-movements do not count as activity, so the pointer does not twitch on camera while you type.

features.title: Timed sessions
features.text: Start Until Turned Off, or 15m / 30m / 1h / 2h / 4h / 8h. When time hits zero, Guard becomes Inactive.

features.title: Idle and jiggle settings
features.text: Choose Idle Threshold (15s–2m) and Jiggle Interval. Settings persist. Guard itself does not turn back on after launch.

features.title: Accessibility onboarding
features.text: The first Session explains why Accessibility is required and opens System Settings. No silent first twitch.

features.title: Privacy-friendly
features.text: No accounts, no tracking. The app works locally. This site is static.

howSubtitle: Idle, then a 1-pixel move and return. That is enough for macOS to treat you as present.

how.title: Start a Session
how.text: Open the menu bar extra. Choose Until Turned Off or a timed duration.

how.title: Stay idle — or keep working
how.text: Typing or moving the mouse resets idle. After the Idle Threshold with no User Activity, a Micro-movement may run.

how.title: Micro-movement
how.text: The pointer moves 1 pixel and returns. Then SessionGuard waits the Jiggle Interval and checks idle again.

quickStartSubtitle: From install to an Active Session in a few minutes.

quickStart.title: Install
quickStart.text: Download the DMG, drag SessionGuard to Applications, and open it.

quickStart.title: Grant Accessibility
quickStart.text: Start a Session. When asked, enable Accessibility in System Settings, then start the Session again.

quickStart.title: Choose duration
quickStart.text: Until Turned Off for an open-ended session, or a timed preset for one meeting.

quickStart.title: Glance the icon
quickStart.text: Filled shield means Active. Remaining time shows during a Timed Session. Outline means Inactive.

faq.question: Why does SessionGuard request Accessibility?
faq.answer: macOS requires Accessibility to synthesize pointer events and to observe keyboard activity without recording keys. Without it, Guard cannot Micro-move.

faq.question: Is my data collected or sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No. This site is static. The app has no accounts and does not send activity data.

faq.question: Does it keep a Mac awake with the lid closed?
faq.answer: No. SessionGuard keeps a login session alive while the Mac is in use with the lid open. It is not a closed-lid server stay-awake tool.

faq.question: Does Guard turn itself back on after login?
faq.answer: No. Launch always starts Inactive, even if Start at Login is on. You start a Session when you need it.

faq.question: Will typing trigger a Micro-movement?
faq.answer: No. Keyboard key-down is User Activity and resets idle. Micro-movements themselves are ignored so they do not retrigger idle.

faq.question: How do I update?
faq.answer: Use Check for Updates… in the SessionGuard menu. The Download button and Sparkle both use the latest GitHub Release.

install: Grant Accessibility when asked, then start a Session
downloadNotice: Free to use — including for businesses.
lookSubtitle: The menu starts a session. Preferences is only idle and interval.

look.title: Two numbers, then Start.
look.text: Idle Threshold and Jiggle Interval. Guard stays Inactive until you start a session — including after login.
